audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer sides were 'Skill' on rows 0-4 while win[] said Xerath, and rows 5-6 said Kassadin while their whys described Xerath winning ('Late Xerath wins fights from the next postal code'). win[6] said Xerath while whys[6] itself says scaling flips to Kassadin.
audit.why: Kassadin is a melee mage with no pre-6 escape — early/mid is Xerath's; with items and stacked Riftwalk (5/3.5/2s base cd) he out-scales, which content spikes[3] and late text already state. Packet levelChart's blanket Xerath x7 contradicts the page's own scaling analysis for the last row.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-5 flipped to Xerath (whys already argue Xerath there, incl. content whys[5] 'poke lead holds at first item'); row 6 kept Kassadin, win[6] flipped to Kassadin to agree, and phases[6].why rewritten to describe Kassadin winning late.

audit.why: Spikes accurate: pre-6 kill window, level 6 Riftwalk, RoA/MR blunting first-item poke, hard late out-scale — all present in spikes[0..3].

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digits; missingInteractions: Kassadin's Null Sphere interrupts channels — it cancels Xerath's R barrage; his combo opens on a Nether Blade auto-reset (the wind-up is the retreat cue); his own Q is also a channel-flagged cast your E can interrupt.
audit.why: enemyKit: Q 'interrupting channels', cd 9-7s, 650 range; W 7s auto-reset; R 5/3.5/2s dash. ownerKit: R channel 'any CC cancels it'.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns rewritten with numbers; Q-interrupts-your-R folded into breakdown.late; auto-reset tell recorded here (no clean in-band anchor).

edits.before: Late Xerath wins fights from the next postal code: stun the entry, barrage the objective, and never be seen.
edits.after: Stacked Riftwalks arrive every 2 seconds late game — Kassadin reaches you through any peel. End before this.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. It governs your forward steps. - E Shocking Orb spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Kassadin Riftwalk (R): 5/3.5/2s base — post-6 it is near-always up; distance, not its cooldown, is your defense. - His Q shield blocks magic briefly — lead with W to pop it, then Q. - Your 13s E spent on poke is a death you scheduled.

edits.before: You are off-screen and decisive: stun the engage, barrage the pit, and re-position before the minimap finds you. Distance is your defense and your damage.
edits.after: Never channel R inside his 650 Q range — Null Sphere interrupts the barrage outright. Stun the Riftwalk arrival, snipe the pit, and stay a screen away.

edits.before: Q the last-hit from beyond his answer range, W the lateral dodge, and walk — a one-way trade he can only end by leaving the lane.
edits.after: Riftwalk covers 500 units; your E reaches 1050 — stun him the instant he blinks in and the all-in he stacked mana for dies on arrival.

edits.before: Spending E on chip and then watching the dash you bought it for arrive on schedule — the stun is your only 'no' and everyone knows it.
edits.after: At half HP a single Riftwalk-W-E combo executes you — the greedy extra Q is exactly the misstep his whole champion was designed to eat.

notes: Chart resolution: rows 0-5 to Xerath (win[] already Xerath there — side-only edits per the decided rule); row 6 kept Kassadin and win[6] flipped Xerath->Kassadin with phases[6].why rewritten to match — content whys[6] already says scaling flips to Kassadin, so all three layers now agree. Packet levelChart claimed Xerath on the last row too; overruled by the page's own consistent scaling analysis and Kassadin's kit. Nether Blade auto-reset as the burst tell had no in-band anchor field; a coach should know the W wind-up, not the spell cast, is the retreat cue. Templated but ungrounded, left alone: breakdown.carry, breakdown.early, breakdown.mid, enemyWin, ahead. phases[5].rating 7/10 and [6].rating 8/10 left as-is; they read as threat ratings and were not clearly wrong.
